ship_list.title: No high-severity bug open
ship_list.note: A high-severity bug holds the release. Medium ones may land after the freeze.

ship_list.title: Every feature merged, moved or cut
ship_list.note: The freeze can be declared once this reaches zero.

ship_list.title: Feature freeze declared
ship_list.note: Only the maintainer declares it, in a comment on the tracker.

ship_list.title: Code-review findings closed
ship_list.note: A blocking finding stays on the milestone. The rest move to the next minor.

ship_list.title: Performance issues closed
ship_list.note: Issues labelled `performance`. A regression against the cycle's baselines is a bug for this milestone; the others may move to the next minor.

ship_list.title: main green for 24 hours
ship_list.note: The candidate needs every push check and nightly job green for a day, Heavy Checks' nightly run included.

ship_list.title: Signed release dry run on main
ship_list.note: The candidate needs one on its exact commit.

ship_list.title: Candidate approved
ship_list.note: The maintainer approves one exact commit on the tracker.

open_issues.title: [FEATURE] Alerts: notify when CPU, memory, temperature or a process crosses a threshold
[Deps] Move the build tooling from Python 3.14 to 3.15 (after #946)
[FEATURE] Publish TaskSmack to Scoop (Extras bucket), kept current by its autoupdate
[FEATURE] Publish tasksmack-bin to the AUR for Arch Linux
perf(windows): Intel's GL driver thread wakes 120 times a second even while TaskSmack is minimized: find out whether our GL state keeps it awake
[Refactor] release.yml is 3,424 lines; split the per-OS jobs into reusable workflows
[Security] VirusTotal and Publisher checks can be fooled by an image overwritten after its section was created (Herpaderping)
[FEATURE] Copy buttons for text fields
[FEATURE] Battery: show the charge or discharge rate, remaining Wh and voltage on both platforms (read, snapshot and battery details)
[FEATURE] Signature, Publisher and VirusTotal for images away from their entry point (.NET Framework, relocated exes) without trusting the process
[FEATURE] Windows uninstaller: optional 'Also remove my settings and themes' (config.toml, themes, lock, log, HKCU key)
[Tooling] Share the agent lanes' rules and merge-gate scripts in the repo (docs/dev/agent-conveyor.md, tools/agent/), with a lane coordination issue
[Perf] The helper availability check walks file security on the startup thread, twice when it fails
[Perf] Three per-sample benchmarks time the probe's start-up workers, not steady state
[Testing] NVML process utilization query misses failure-path coverage
[Tracker] C++23 audit (main a6b09132): toolchain facts and findings
[Refactor] Clang's thread-safety analysis is unused: 263 lock uses and no GUARDED_BY, though libc++'s std::mutex is already annotated
[Refactor] Four warning suppressions are wider than what they were added for
[Testing] About 185 lines of GPU-reset recovery are excluded from coverage as 'no test can cause a reset', but most of them need no reset to run
[Testing] 70 broker tests skip when the broker refuses the test's user, and nothing in CI turns that skip into a failure
[Testing] Seven tests assert an upper bound on elapsed wall-clock time, the shape of 20 past CI flakes
[Testing] Nine 'nothing happens' tests sleep a fixed time and then assert a count of zero, so a starved sampler passes them vacuously
[Testing] Tests set and restore environment variables by hand: one drops the real XDG_SESSION_ID, and a failed ASSERT leaks a changed HOME into every later test
[Refactor] runApp() in main.cpp is a 670-line function whose security-relevant start-up order is held only by comments; no test or coverage run reaches it
[Refactor] OpenedImage owns a raw void* file handle, so its callers hand-write the cleanup (a try/catch and two ordering comments)
[Testing] The Windows HTTPS client's reply-size cap and multi-chunk body loop have no test; the Linux client's cap does
[Refactor] 168 NOLINT comments in src/ name clang-tidy checks that .clang-tidy disables for the whole project
[Refactor] Four Windows version-resource readers with four sets of rules; the by-handle reader exists and three don't use it
[Refactor] Windows: the process snapshot is grown in three loops and walked by four parsers, and WindowsProcessProbe keeps a private TCP-table reader
[Perf] Text is still rebuilt every frame at ten sites, one of them a heap allocation per frame in every unelevated Windows session
[Refactor] Five action views are implicitly movable while their in-flight finish callbacks capture this
[Refactor] Modal dialog state is three bools re-declared in seven dialogs, and the affinity dialog lacks a reset its twin has
[Refactor] Three different 'same process?' rules over ProcessTarget, built on start time 0 meaning 'unknown'
[Refactor] AccelNpuProbe computes the NPU's utilization percent itself and keeps the baseline in the probe
[Refactor] NetlinkSocketStats runs a throwaway warm-up dump at start and keeps a mutex and two public methods for callers that don't exist
[Testing] Eleven real-kernel tests in test_NetlinkSocketStats.cpp can't fail, and nothing checks a real connection's byte counters
[Testing] LinuxProcessProbe and NetlinkSocketStats read steady_clock directly, so their cadence tests sleep and skip themselves under load
[Refactor] Linux dead code: the TASKSMACK_HAS_NETLINK_SOCKET_STATS == 0 build no longer compiles, and DRMGPUProbe's uevent name branch can't run
[Refactor] Linux: 'open a pidfd, then verify the start time' is hand-repeated at 11 sites, around a result struct whose two fields can disagree
[Refactor] Linux: two hand-written posix_spawn runners have drifted; the dump runner lacks the RAII and the child guard the other has
[Refactor] 16 std::strerror calls sit under concurrency-mt-unsafe NOLINTs with wrong or missing reasons; std::generic_category().message() is already used beside them
[Testing] NaN reaches std::clamp and float-to-integer casts in five formatting helpers; the CPU chart's gap depends on it, and no test pins either
[Refactor] The 'interval too short to rate' threshold is declared three times, with two different rules
[Perf] Nine CI benchmarks time HistoryBuffer, which no production code uses; SharedHistoryBuffer, on every model's hot path, has none
[Refactor] Main-tab identity is a string literal repeated at about 25 sites; a typo silently disables a tab
[Refactor] Linux: App has re-grown two owning-descriptor classes and three hand-closed descriptors after #1183 gave Platform one FdGuard
[Refactor] Six pairs of fields that only make sense together are stored separately (window position, hand-off PID and start time, resize step, and others)
[Refactor] LazyBackgroundRead::start() relabels the in-flight read with the new target before it knows a new read started
[Testing] Re-attaching a panel or layer is described in comments but never tested, and three latent hazards sit on that path
[Testing] SessionAccountCheck::wait()'s 30-second timeout, which fails open to 'same account', has no test and no seam
[Refactor] BrokerRequestMapping dispatches with std::get_if chains, so a request kind with no handler compiles and answers 'Not an action' at run time
[Refactor] 22 probe and reader interfaces have public defaulted copy and move, so assigning through a base reference slices; the 8 newer ones delete them
[Refactor] Theme metadata and colours live in duplicate structs and parallel vectors, and every theme file is parsed twice at startup on the UI thread
[Refactor] UserConfig.cpp compiles all 3,900 lines of UI/ChartWidgets.h (ImGui, ImPlot, chart templates) to reach two setters
[Refactor] Nine call sites use Dear ImGui names that the pinned 1.93 marks obsolete; they compile only while IMGUI_DISABLE_OBSOLETE_FUNCTIONS is off
[Refactor] Nine helpers still return a flag or a sentinel beside out-parameters; std::expected, used 359 times already, makes success and failure exclusive
[Refactor] Dead code found by the audit: fourteen functions, members and branches that nothing in src/ reaches
[FEATURE] No release check enforces the glibc 2.38 floor the docs promise
[FEATURE] The RPM is half-supported: the FAQ says an .rpm installs the Administrator launcher, none is published, and a local RPM has CMake's default metadata and no hand-added Requires
[BUG] The .deb is validated with Recommends installed, and the .tar.gz and the user guide's dependency list are never tested on their own
[FEATURE] publish-winget submits wingetcreate's manifests after checking only ManifestVersion, and rehearse-winget's comment says it checks more
[FEATURE] Nothing detects drift between the packaging/winget templates and the manifests wingetcreate carries forward
[FEATURE] The wingetcreate pin isn't tracked, and comments calling v1.12.13.0 "the newest release" are stale
[FEATURE] The ARP entry lacks InstallLocation and EstimatedSize
[FEATURE] No release check reads the version the packaged binary reports
[FEATURE] The draft is published after a name and size check only; digests are compared only after the release is public
[FEATURE] No release gate checks that libsystemd/sd-bus and libcurl were built in
[FEATURE] Linux upgrades are tested only from v0.8.0 on x64, never from the previous release or on arm64
[FEATURE] No AppStream metainfo ships
[FEATURE] desktop-file-validate never runs on the shipped .desktop files
[FEATURE] The released BPF object is never loaded in the release workflow
[FEATURE] The .deb declares none of the optional tools it uses (xdg-utils, strace, gdb)
[FEATURE] The .tar.gz's dependency line gives Debian/Ubuntu package names only, and libbpf is a hard dependency for an opt-in, root-only feature
[FEATURE] The theme count is hard-coded in the WinGet description, the user guide and the README, and wingetcreate carries the old description forward
[Testing] Eight test types have external linkage only because of the old 'mocks outside an anonymous namespace' rule; move them in and drop the NOLINTs that defend it
[FEATURE] Native scripts on each platform: agent:Windows writes and runs PowerShell, agent:WSL bash, and the conveyor's gate scripts move into tools/ as .ps1/.sh pairs
[FEATURE] Release Command Center phase 3: what makes main red, stage durations and per-lane speed, plus two leftovers from #4524
[BUG] Make sure Events use the Event system
[Performance] The Processes table builds its folded sort keys on every sort, not once per sample
[BUG] Deleting tasksmack.lock while TaskSmack runs lets a second copy start on the same settings folder
[FEATURE] Interaction polish from the manual pass: no confirm for Resume, state-aware Suspend/Resume, errors that stay, PID filter, Check now tooltip
[BUG] Release dashboard: during CI bursts every job waits minutes for a runner whatever its label, and a dashboard run needs one twice
[FEATURE] Windows: name SYSTEM/service/DWM processes' accounts in a Standard session from their service's configured account and their session
[Refactor] LinuxHeldFolder: RAII for DIR*/lock fd, std::optional instead of the posixFolderFd() -1 sentinel, and one save path instead of the unreachable replaceFile()
[DOCS] LinuxProcessActions::dumpFolderAccess()'s doc says NotChecked as root, but root returns AdministratorsOnly when the user can't open the folder
[REFACTOR] SessionUser: processHoldsAmbientCapabilities() copies processHoldsCapabilities()'s /proc/self/status parse
[REFACTOR] SystemdUnitActions: loadUnitRead() duplicates unitPath()'s LoadUnit call and reply handling
[Security] Scorecard Binary-Artifacts: the fuzz_version_resource seeds start with a PE header; generate them at build time instead
[FEATURE] Release dashboard: a checklist item whose issue moved to another milestone or was closed as not planned shows as moved or dropped, not open
[Testing] At v0.11.1's release: an installed 0.11.0 notices 0.11.1 (in-app update check and button), upgrades in place, and WinGet upgrades it
[Tooling] release.ps1 -Step Bump leaves 'Fixes #<tracker>' for a person to fill in; find the [RELEASE X.Y.Z] tracker itself and link it with 'Part of'
[BUG] sandbox-install-check.ps1 reports 'Runs for 15 s: PASS' when TaskSmack is stuck on an OpenGL error dialog; its .wsb doesn't turn the vGPU on
[FEATURE] [BUG] Sensors should be live data tied to their components
